headline: Haaland double powers Man City to 2-0 victory over Porto
summary: Erling Haaland scored twice to secure a win for Manchester City in their Champions League opener, becoming the club's third highest all-time goalscorer.
details: Erling Haaland scored twice as Manchester City began their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 victory at Porto.
Despite a strong first-half performance by Porto's goalkeeper Diogo Costa, Haaland broke the deadlock early in the second half with a downward header.
Haaland sealed the win in stoppage time, clinically slotting the ball into the bottom corner to reach 167 goals for City, making him the third highest goalscorer of all-time for the club.
The match served as a positive start for new manager Enzo Maresca, who has succeeded Pep Guardiola.
Maresca's side featured the first start for Ayyoub Bouaddi, who joined City from Lille for 100 million euros.
While City dominated the early stages, they faced pressure from Porto in the second half, with goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma nearly conceding a penalty after a foul on Pepe.
Haaland continues his prolific form, having netted five goals in his first four games of the new campaign.
caption:
Erling Haaland does it again! A double from the Norwegian striker powers Manchester City

Erling Haaland scored twice as Manchester City began their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 victory at Porto.

Despite a strong first-half performance by Porto's goalkeeper Diogo Costa, Haaland broke the deadlock early in the second half with a downward header.

Haaland sealed the win in stoppage time, clinically slotting the ball into the bottom corner to reach 167 goals for City, making him the third highest goalscorer of all-time for the club.

The match served as a positive start for new manager Enzo Maresca, who has succeeded Pep Guardiola.

Maresca's side featured the first start for Ayyoub Bouaddi, who joined City from Lille for 100 million euros.

While City dominated the early stages, they faced pressure from Porto in the second half, with goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma nearly conceding a penalty after a foul on Pepe.

Haaland continues his prolific form, having netted five goals in his first four games of the new campaign.

headline_marked: Govt to [[bring Benazir Ahmed back]] from UAE for trial
headline: Govt to bring Benazir Ahmed back from UAE for trial
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed assured Parliament that no leniency will be shown in bringing back fugitive fugitives like former IGP Benazir Ahmed.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told the National Parliament on Tuesday that the government will show no leniency in bringing back fugitive suspects, including former IGP Benazir Ahmed, to face trial.
The Minister stated that the government is coordinating with Interpol and various diplomatic missions to ensure the extradition of those residing abroad.

Benazir Ahmed, who served as the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner during the operation against Hefazat-e-Islam at Shapla Chattar, later faced allegations of enforced disappearances, illegal asset acquisition, and corruption while serving as IGP.
Following the 2024 mass uprising, Benazir left the country. Reports that he has been detained in Dubai have led to urgent calls in Parliament for his extradition.
Members of Parliament from various parties, including Jamaat-e-Islami and BNP, demanded strong action to bring him back for trial to ensure accountability for victims.
Proposals were made to form a special cell dedicated to identifying and bringing back fugitives residing abroad.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir noted that extradition is being considered on a case-by-case basis and diplomatic pressure will be applied where necessary.
Additionally, the government is working to verify allegations regarding multiple passports and identify and seize illegally acquired assets both domestically and internationally.
caption:
No leniency for fugitives. The government is coordinating with Interpol to bring former IGP Benazir Ahmed back from the UAE.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told the National Parliament on Tuesday that the government will show no leniency in bringing back fugitive suspects, including former IGP Benazir Ahmed, to face trial.

The Minister stated that the government is coordinating with Interpol and various diplomatic missions to ensure the extradition of those residing abroad.

Benazir Ahmed, who served as the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner during the operation against Hefazat-e-Islam at Shapla Chattar, later faced allegations of enforced disappearances, illegal asset acquisition, and corruption while serving as IGP.

Following the 2024 mass uprising, Benazir left the country. Reports that he has been detained in Dubai have led to urgent calls in Parliament for his extradition.

Members of Parliament from various parties, including Jamaat-e-Islami and BNP, demanded strong action to bring him back for trial to ensure accountability for victims.

Proposals were made to form a special cell dedicated to identifying and bringing back fugitives residing abroad.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir noted that extradition is being considered on a case-by-case basis and diplomatic pressure will be applied where necessary.

Additionally, the government is working to verify allegations regarding multiple passports and identify and seize illegally acquired assets both domestically and internationally.
